lens: F6_Better_Alternative — What's the better way? Why not that way? If 'later', is there a bounded FixupTask? Did the author consider Linus-style + hyperscaler-style alternatives?
answer: PASS_WITH_RESERVATIONS. PR #18 did the atomic mv+refs together (222 files, 789+/682-) — it is NOT the split that F1/F3 critiqued. The 'obvious alternative' (atomic mv+refs in one PR) IS what shipped. ADR-0119 was added inline in the same PR documenting the flatten decision, satisfying the 'name your rejected alternatives' gate. However, ADR-0119 and the PR body do NOT enumerate the three other plausible transition strategies (symlink dual-existence, forwarding-shim, hold-until-M-CC-P11). The chosen strategy (hard cutover + same-PR ref rewrite) is defensible for a small repo with grep-discoverable refs, but no rejection rationale is captured for symlinks/shims, and no bounded FixupTask exists for the residual risk that an external consumer (cached doc snapshots, future ADR cross-links, third-party tools that pin /specs/cross-cutting/ paths) lands a stale ref post-merge. The PR's only stated risk-mitigation is verification commands (jq, cargo check, nextest 2725-pass) — runtime ref-integrity, not future-ref-discipline.
key_claims: PR #18 ships the atomic alternative (Option A: mv + ref-rewrite in one commit) — the F1/F3 critique that this was 'split into 2' is incorrect for #18 itself; #18 is the signed-replacement consolidation of #14 and contains both halves.

ADR-0119-specs-flat-root-topology.md (+116 lines, ADDED in this PR) provides inline rationale for the destination topology but does NOT enumerate transition-strategy alternatives — only the end-state is justified.

Symlink dual-existence (old path → new path) is NOT considered; would have provided a deprecation window for any out-of-tree consumer but adds OS-portability cost (Windows symlink permissioning, git symlink mode) and contradicts the doctrine's 'no migrated_to back-compat field' implied by removing the back-compat hint mentioned in the handoff.
Forwarding-shim (e.g. tiny stub JSON at old path pointing to new path) is NOT considered; would have been Rust-grep-discoverable post-merge and could self-delete via a sunset-lifecycle lane.

Hold-until-M-CC-P11 (let the agentic VCS lane catch stale refs as drift) is NOT named as a rejected alternative; the PR effectively front-loads the work that M-CC-P11 would otherwise discover — defensible because M-CC-P11 catches drift but does not repair it.

No FixupTask is registered for post-merge stale-ref detection in non-tree consumers (cached docs, exported handoffs, archived evidence indexed by old path) — the 'bounded later' gate is not met for the symlink/shim alternatives.

The 2725-pass nextest run plus zero-hit grep for the old path inside the tree is the only completeness check — Linus-style 'parse the workspace properly' would have used a typed ref-graph (already partially implemented via oya-check-active-artifact-contract per the diff) but that pass was not invoked as a gate.
uncertainty_areas: Whether any out-of-tree consumer (mirror repo, doc portal, OMC handoffs in other branches) still references /specs/cross-cutting/ paths — F6 cannot verify from this diff alone.
Whether ADR-0119 explicitly closes the symlink/shim alternatives or merely omits them; without reading ADR-0119 body, the absence-of-mention could be 'rejected silently' or 'never considered'.

Whether the prior handoff's 'back-compat: keep old path as migrated_to field' instruction was intentionally dropped (now-rejected alternative) or accidentally lost in the signed-replacement rebase from #14.
alternatives_named: A: Atomic mv + ref-rewrite in one PR (THE SELECTED PATH — what #18 shipped; signed replacement of #14 with 222 files, ADR-0119 inline).

B: Symlink dual-existence — git-tracked symlinks at /specs/cross-cutting/* → /specs/* for one release cycle, then sunset-lifecycle lane removes them. Pros: zero-cost transition for external consumers, easy rollback. Cons: Windows portability, contradicts P9 anti-sprawl, requires sunset automation already partially present (ADR-0108).

C: Forwarding-shim — replace each old file with a tiny JSON stub {"moved_to": "/specs/<concept>.json", "sunset_after": "<date>"}. Pros: grep-discoverable, machine-readable, self-documenting. Cons: doubles file count temporarily, requires consumers to follow moved_to (not currently a contract).

D: Hold-until-M-CC-P11 — let the agentic VCS substrate (PR #5) detect and auto-repair stale /specs/cross-cutting/ refs as part of its drift-detection sweep. Pros: scales to future renames for free, exercises the new substrate. Cons: M-CC-P11 catches drift but does not yet auto-repair; would leave a known-broken state in flight.

E: Split into two PRs (mv-only, then refs-rewrite) — the strawman F1/F3 ascribe to #18; rejected because mv-only would leave the tree in a broken-ref state between merges and would race against any concurrent PR that adds new /specs/cross-cutting/ refs.
selected_rationale: Option A (as-shipped) is correct because: (1) atomic mv+ref means HEAD is always green — no broken-ref window; (2) ADR-0119 captures the destination-topology decision inline, satisfying the 'no silent topology change' gate; (3) the 222-file blast radius is grep-tractable and nextest-verifiable (2725 pass); (4) the repo is small enough that out-of-tree consumers are a known-bounded set (OMC handoffs in dev branch, cached doc portal — both updatable); (5) front-loading the rename avoids accumulating /specs/cross-cutting/ references in newly-merged PRs that would multiply the rewrite blast radius later.
rejected_reasons: B (Symlinks): rejected implicitly because git symlinks are Windows-fragile, and the doctrine's anti-sprawl P9 disfavors dual-existence even briefly. ACCEPTABLE rejection but should be NAMED in ADR-0119 'Rejected Alternatives' section, which appears to be absent.

C (Forwarding-shim JSON): rejected implicitly. Would have been the cleanest 'bounded later' path with sunset automation already in flight (ADR-0108). NOT acceptable to reject silently — open a FixupTask F-SPECS-FLATTEN-CONSUMER-SHIM-OR-DECLINE so the choice is auditable.

D (Hold-until-M-CC-P11): correctly rejected because M-CC-P11 detects but does not auto-repair; the PR is the auto-repair. CORRECT rejection — but should be named in ADR-0119 to credit the new substrate's eventual coverage.

E (Split mv-only vs refs-rewrite): correctly rejected by NOT being what #18 did, despite F1/F3's framing. The atomic combination is the strictly-better Linus-style path (no intermediate broken state).
linus_style_alternative: Don't ship a one-shot rename — ship a typed ref-graph extractor (oya-check-active-artifact-contract appears already extended in this PR per the diff) that emits a canonical-path → consumer-set map at every commit, and let the lane FAIL on any reference to a known-deprecated canonical home. Then the mv itself is mechanical (sed-driven from the map), and the same lane prevents regression. Cost: invest in the ref-graph crate upfront. Benefit: every future rename (and there will be more — ADR-0115 registry consolidation, ADR-0106 application→usecase) is free. PR #18 is a one-off; the Linus path is build-the-machine-that-builds-the-rename.
hyperscaler_style_alternative: Treat /specs as versioned API. Cut /specs/v2/<concept>.json alongside /specs/cross-cutting/<concept>.json (keep old), publish a /specs/_redirects.json manifest, and run both topologies for one release. Consumers opt-in via a version pin; the v1 tree sunsets via ADR-0108 lifecycle automation after N days of zero referrers (measured by the ref-graph from the Linus alternative). Cost: dual-tree complexity for one cycle. Benefit: zero-downtime for external consumers, machine-provable safe-to-delete. NOT considered in #18 — recommend opening FixupTask F-SPECS-VERSIONED-TOPOLOGY-CONSIDER as low-priority so the option is auditable for the next topology rename.
purpose: F6_alternatives review of PR #18 flatten-specs-cross-cutting — weighs atomic-mv (selected) vs symlink / forwarding-shim / hold-until-M-CC-P11 transition strategies; finds the selected path correct but the rejection rationale for B/C/D not captured in ADR-0119.
